newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Organic growth seen for Bank of Scotland.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Organic growth seen for Bank of Scotland.

text.p: Bank of Scotland Governor Sir Bruce Pattullo said on Thursday he expects to see the bank's Australia and New Zealand operations grow organically rather than through more acquisitions.
Bank of Scotland now owns 51 percent of Bank of Western Australia (BankWest) and owns New Zealand's Countrywide Bank outright. It also has two smaller businesses in Sydney.
"We've got enough businesses here and what we need to do is grow them organically and build them up," Pattullo said in an interview.
"Over the years, that is what Bank of Scotland has been good at doing, so I don't envisage us rushing to make further acquisitions in this part of the world," Pattullo said.
"We see interesting long-term possibilities. The growth prospects, compared with some of the more mature economies, are very interesting."
Perth-based BankWest said last month that its profit for the year to February 28 was likely to be five percent below its prospectus forecast of A$100.2 million.
But Pattullo said the news had not dampened Bank of Scotland's enthusiasm for the investment, adding the lower outcome had emanated from the current mortgage war in Australia.

Asked if this was likely to be a temporary setback for BankWest, Pattullo said: "It clearly depends on what is going to happen in the mortgage market in Australia." Whether the principal players there were likely to pare back rates further in the name of competition was yet to be seen.
"I don't think it alters in any way our enthusiasm for the acquisition of BankWest in the longer term. These are the tactical issues that you come up against in any market."
Bank of Scotland recently opened a representative office in Singapore, a reflection of the number of its customers in Australia and New Zealand with trade relationships in Asia.
But the bank nevertheless felt that it needed a greater understanding of Asia-Pacific markets.
Pattullo said Bank of Scotland's joint venture with British supermarket group J. Sainsbury Plc had been up and running for just three weeks after gaining a licence in early February.
Sainbury's has a 55 percent holding in Sainsbury's Bank and Bank of Scotland the remainder.

Pattullo said the move was made to capitalise on the Bank of Scotland's extensive telephone banking operations, which would now be complemented by the Sainsbury's chain. He added it was possible Countrywide may choose to forge a similar allliance.
While many in the industry maintained New Zealand was overbanked, Pattullo disagreed.
"It's easier for the smaller player to take market share off the bigger player than for the bigger player to go on increasing it," he said.
"Bank of Scotland is in a roughly comparable situation (to Countrywide) in the U.K.," he said, adding the bank had increased its share over each of the last 15 years or so.
